data.text:
Fact Check : Indonesia Never Sank “Chinese Vessels”

False claim spotted again.
Vietnamese account @NguyenThih36 is recycling an old video of Indonesia’s anti-illegal fishing campaign and falsely claiming China was the target.

Let’s unpack the facts (and the clickbait pattern) 

Since 2014, Indonesia has indeed destroyed hundreds of illegal fishing boats.
But according to official data from Indonesia’s Ministry of Maritime Affairs (Tempo & Antara reports), the overwhelming majority were from:
• 🇻🇳 Vietnam: 294+
• 🇵🇭 Philippines: 92
• 🇲🇾 Malaysia: 76
• 🇹🇭 Thailand: 23
• 🇮🇩 Indonesia (domestic): 26

Only one vessel was recorded from China. Just one.

The explosion footage shown in the video?
📍It’s from 2017, during a mass sinking of 81 boats.
🔍 Breakdown of targets in that operation:
• 46 Vietnamese
• 18 Philippine
• 11 Malaysian
• 6 Indonesian (domestic illegal operations)

No Chinese vessels were sunk.
Indonesia was targeting its immediate neighbors, not China.

Let’s talk clickbait strategy:
• First post: Nov 21, 2025 — 799K views
• Same video reposted: Dec 16, 2025 — 925.5K views

Same lie, same explosion, just more outrage farming.
This isn’t journalism. It’s a scam for engagement.

The narrative that Indonesia is “teaching China a lesson” is not only false, it’s a cheap attempt to sow hostility between nations.

You know what’s ironic?
The biggest number of boats destroyed were from… Vietnam.
And yet it’s a Vietnamese account pretending to cheer Indonesia on for sinking Chinese vessels.

The irony is almost poetic.
